pages.text: "Mom, I want to call out!" Coco, in a red headscarf, held a bread basket just inside the door. Mom opened it. "All right. Call loudly into the alley, 'The bread is ready!'"
People passed through the alley outside. Coco opened their mouth, then pressed it shut. "Everyone might look at me..." Coco slipped behind the door.
Behind the door, Coco's heart thumped. "Aren't you going to, Coco?" Mom asked from the kitchen. "I just... won't." Coco pouted. The bread in the basket was cooling.
Jingle! Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, came in. He sat beside Coco behind the door and whispered, "Feeling shy? I do too. Shall we start softly?"
"Just say it in my ear." Grandpa leaned his ear close. Coco whispered very softly, "The bread... is ready..." Grandpa smiled wide. "I heard you! Softly first, then loudly!"
Grandpa held Coco's paw at the doorstep. "This time, together." They called a little louder. "The bread is ready!" People simply walked past. Coco's mouth began to smile.
Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws and took one step into the alley. A deep breath, then out came the words. "The bread is ready!" The voice reached the end of the alley. Grandpa clapped.

From the far end of the alley, people came toward the bakery, one by one. Mom came out of the kitchen and smiled at Coco. "They heard your voice!" Coco straightened proudly, smiling wide. "I... did it!"

The next day, Coco called straight from the doorstep. "The bread is ready! One, say I'm shy! Two, start softly! Three, move forward one spot at a time!" Whenever Coco felt shy, they counted these three steps.
Grandpa sat beside Coco and warmly wrapped an arm around their shoulders. "It's okay to be shy. Starting softly will get you there." Looking at the alley, Coco called, "Softly first, then loudly!"
